rendered_html: 📔 Regulatory Bulletin — 27 October 2026 (Daily) Executive Summary • The SFC approved the first secondary trading of two tokenised public money-market funds on a licensed virtual-asset platform. This is a live application of the April pilot framework, so investment and digital-asset businesses should monitor scope, pricing, liquidity and disclosure implications rather than treat it as a new sector-wide obligation. • HSBC launched HSBCnio for corporate and institutional transaction banking, combining existing-permission web/mobile access, APIs and read-only access by client AI tools to authorised account and transaction data. The launch is a commercial benchmark for treasury-channel, data-access and AI/API control design, not a Hong Kong regulatory change. Hong Kong 🟡 SFC approves first-ever secondary trading of tokenised public funds 🇭🇰 Item ID: item-20261026-sfc-web-26pr174 ⏰ Deadline: No source deadline stated Products: Tokenised funds; virtual-asset trading; digital payments On 26 October 2026, the Securities and Futures Commission approved secondary trading of two existing SFC-authorised tokenised money-market funds on an SFC-licensed virtual-asset trading platform, with around-the-clock trading beginning that day. The SFC states that its April 2026 pilot framework sets requirements and safeguards for trading-channel operation, fair pricing, liquidity provision and disclosure. This is the first stated live approval under that existing pilot rather than a new rule or a direct instruction to institutions outside the approved arrangement; the SFC will monitor activity and may consider broader product scope. Banks with authorised-fund, digital-asset distribution, tokenised-deposit or settlement roles may need to monitor whether a future expansion affects their product, disclosure, pricing, liquidity, settlement or 24/7 operating model. Source: SFC approves first-ever secondary trading of tokenised public funds 🟡 HSBC launches new AI-enabled solution to transform transaction banking 🇭🇰 Item ID: item-20261026-hk-banks-news-808c29cdd6 ⏰ Deadline: No source deadline stated Products: Transaction banking; APIs; corporate treasury On 26 October 2026, HSBC announced HSBCnio, an AI-enabled transaction-banking solution for corporate and institutional clients that supports web/mobile access through existing HSBCnet credentials and permissions, as well as API connections to client systems. HSBC says client AI tools can access authorised account and transaction data on a read-only basis through its Model Context Protocol, using established permissions and appropriate controls. Stated use cases include cash and transaction views, trade loans, FX, payment tracking and cross-border cash analysis; HSBC says the planned Ask HSBC feature is not yet current. This is a peer-bank product announcement, not a Hong Kong regulatory change, approval or sector-wide obligation, but it provides a commercial/control benchmark for permissions, customer-data access, API integration and AI/vendor governance in corporate treasury workflows. Source: HSBC launches new AI-enabled solution to transform transaction banking Mainland/GBA No validated items for this run. SG/UK/GLOBAL Benchmark Comparable overseas developments and commercial/control benchmarks. They do not establish Hong Kong requirements. No validated items for this run. Watch List • Monitor whether the SFC broadens the tokenised-fund pilot beyond the approved arrangement, including the products and participant roles covered. • Monitor whether HSBC introduces write-capable AI functions or publishes customer, jurisdictional or control terms for HSBCnio.
